name: the_walk
revision: r3 (2026-11-11): batch-2 script session. The audit's must-changes (docs/pitches/batch2_premise_audit_2026-11-11.md): 'Mom says that means NEVER.' after the promise; Grandma on screen (her figure in a lit 3x2 window at FOV 20, and in the boat in the flashback); the island 60 blocks from the dock's end in every shot; the trade tooltip as an engine gap with 'Frost Walker II' in the captions. Current format: Pip one_take, character lines with a one-clause bracket, shows, punch, upload, family. Grandma's promise is now her own line (L07) in her own voice. See reviews/r3-*.md
caption: grandpa broke the same lectern 3,000 times 📚
logline: A grandpa has broken the same librarian's lectern three thousand times, rerolling her book; ten years ago Grandma left for the island across the bay and told him to walk the water to her or not come at all, and this morning the book is Frost Walker II.
question: why tf has grandpa broken the same lectern 3,000 times?
premise: Grandpa has broken the same lectern three thousand times: the librarian holds up a book, he reads it, 'Not THAT one', and breaks the lectern again. Grandma lives on the island across the bay; her window is lit every night. He won't take a boat or build a bridge, ten years. When she left, in a boat, she told him: 'Walk the water to me. Or don't come.' Mom says that means never.
twist: He's been rerolling the librarian for one book, Frost Walker (vanilla: breaking a librarian's lectern before you ever trade with her changes the book she offers; Frost Walker freezes water under your feet). Everyone heard 'never'; he took it literally. This morning the trade screen reads Frost Walker II, Grandpa says nothing, and he walks off the end of the dock as the sea freezes under every step, a white path toward Grandma in her lit window. Cut.

requests.direction: One continuous telling, start to finish: bright and quick, a kid who thinks Grandpa is a funny old crank; no dramatic pauses, the last line a little slower.

[An old woman, stubborn and teasing, a small smile]

lines.text: My GRANDPA / has BROKEN / the same LECTERN / three thousand TIMES.
lines.say: My grandpa has broken the same lectern three thousand times.
lines.direction: amazed and fed up, one quick breath; the number lands

lines.text: The LIBRARIAN / holds up a BOOK. / He READS it. / Breaks the LECTERN / AGAIN.
lines.say: The librarian holds up a book. He reads it. Breaks the lectern again.
lines.direction: rhythmic, a routine she has watched a thousand times

lines.text: GRANDMA lives / on the ISLAND / across the BAY. / Her WINDOW'S lit / every NIGHT.
lines.say: Grandma lives on the island across the bay. Her window's lit every night.

lines.text: He WON'T / take a BOAT. / Won't BUILD / a BRIDGE. / Ten YEARS.
lines.say: He won't take a boat. Won't build a bridge. Ten years.
lines.direction: baffled and a little funny; the last two words land
lines.note: 'bridge' is a thing he won't build: nothing to show (the open sea between dock and island is the picture)

lines.text: When she LEFT, / she TOLD him:
lines.say: When she left, she told him:
lines.direction: leaning in, telling the family legend; straight into her line

lines.text: Walk the WATER / to ME. / Or don't COME.
lines.say: Walk the water to me. Or don't come.
lines.direction: stubborn and teasing, a dare with a small smile; the last word lands
matter-of-fact, a kid repeating what grown-ups say

lines.text: This MORNING, / the LIBRARIAN / held UP / a NEW book.
lines.say: This morning, the librarian held up a new book.
lines.direction: quick, noticing; a lift on the key word
surprised, a little slower, the last word held
